title: Former Savoy College Students Ready For 14th Annual Reunion
text:
Former Savoy College Students Ready For 14th Annual Reunion

(Herald News Service)

SAVOY—Sixty-five of the 131 survivors who attended Savoy College have indicated they plan to attend the 14th annual reunion set for Savoy Sunday, according to Ed A. McMahon of Dallas president of the Savoy College Ex-Student Association.

The vanguard of this group, however, will move into Savoy shortly after lunch Saturday for an informal program that will start at 3 p.m. This is strictly just an old-fashion "chinfest" by former students who have been getting together once a year since 1938 when they organized the association.

Savoy College was chartered in 1880 and had become one of the leading colleges in this area when it burned July 3, 1890. Attempts to revive it failed.

The headquarters for the reunion is the Halsell Memorial Gymnasium, the school building that was named after the founder of the college.

Officers, in addition to President McMahon, include vice presidents John Umphress, H. L. Davis, Benton Maxey, Thomas E. Crabb, and Tom H. Smith; Jessie Gorrell Young, secretary-treasurer; Pamela Paxton Boyd, historian-librarian; and Gus W. Thomasson, Beulah Thomasson Stinnett and Lillian Durrett King, board of managers.

During the past year, seven committees have functioned in keeping the organization intact. Lloyd Hunnicutt, Will H. Davis and O. O. Suddath composed the auditing committee; Mrs. Jessie Young, Gus Thomasson and Mrs. Lillie King put out the monthly news bulletins.

The resolutions committee included J. B. Maxcy, Mrs. W. H. Davis, Mrs. Lee Gregory and Tom Hickman. Mrs. W. F. Dodd, Mrs. L. S. Sivells, Mrs. J. R. Maxwell and John McClure made up the necrology committee.

Benton Roberts, Mrs. Dora Fowler, Mrs. S. H. Reed and Fred Harle operated as the nominations committee and prepared a slate of officers that will be voted on Sunday.

Music for the reunion was arranged by Mrs. Claude Hodge, Mrs. L. J. Reynolds, Mrs. W. P. Carter, Mrs. J. F. Lawrence, Mrs. B. F. Matthews and Fred Hare. The constitution and by-laws committee was made up of Judge J. B. Maxcy, Mrs. W. L. Whedbee, Mrs. V. E. Conway, Mrs. W. F. Blanton, and Mrs. Charlton McCaughey.

PARTLY CLOUDY

FOR TEXOMALAND: Continued partly cloudy and warm. Winds will be from the south at 15-20 miles per hour. Low tonight will be 74 degrees with a high of 95 degrees Saturday.
notes: Weather box 'PARTLY CLOUDY' for Texomaland appears in lower left column. Article date is likely 1952 based on '14th annual' reunion and the companion 1951 article referencing the same event.
